subject.title: Feature request: first-class .env / environment-backed secret config UX

question: What SecretRef source metadata may Control UI expose for env-backed secrets, and should env variable names or resolved/unresolved state be shown by default?
rationale: The requested UX improves secret hygiene, but exposing env variable names, provider aliases, or resolution state can reveal operator setup details, so automation should not choose that disclosure boundary alone.

options.title: Conservative source-aware UI
options.body: Show masked SecretRef source labels and resolved/unresolved state, reveal env variable names only where maintainers approve, and keep writes aligned with existing SecretRef configure/apply paths.

options.title: Minimal read-only badge
options.body: Replace the generic empty placeholder with a safe configured-SecretRef badge while leaving source switching and env identity for a later design.

options.title: Defer UI disclosure
options.body: Keep the current read-only Control UI behavior and improve CLI/docs guidance until security review defines a fuller metadata policy.

recommendation.title: Conservative source-aware UI
recommendation.body: Show masked SecretRef source labels and resolved/unresolved state, reveal env variable names only where maintainers approve, and keep writes aligned with existing SecretRef configure/apply paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Josh authored the merged SecretRef hardening path that already connects Control UI rendering, config write preflight, redaction, and docs.
